extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry / homological algebra (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Working through textbook material and exercises on limits/colimits, adjoint functors, additive/abelian categories, complexes, exactness of functors, and basic spectral-sequence context; aimed at building facility with definitions, examples, and routine proofs.  Focus is on understanding constructions (e.g., colimits of modules), verifying universal properties, and proving standard propositions (e.g., long exact sequence, FHHF theorem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Colimit of A-modules (general diagram)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a diagram F : I → ModA, the colimit is the direct sum ⊕i Mi quotiented by the submodule generated by relations mi − F(n)(mi) for every arrow n : i → j in I (here Mi := F(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Modulo" means quotiented by the submodule generated by those elements. (Exercise 1.4.G: construct this and verify universal property.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal interpretation of limits and colimits (set-like categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 'set-like' categories, an element of a limit is a family of elements, one from each object of the diagram, which are 'compatible' along the maps; an element of a colimit has a representative coming from a single object in the diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exercises 1.4.B and 1.4.D for precise verification; keep these pictures in mind when reasoning about limits/colimits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of adjoint functors
rubrics_metrics.description: Two covariant functors F : A → B and G : B → A are adjoint if there is a natural bijection τ_{A,B}: Mor_B(F(A), B) ≅ Mor_A(A, G(B)) for all objects A in A and B in B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naturality means certain diagrams (given in (1.5.0.2)) commute for all morphisms f and g; exercises 1.5.A and 1.5.B ask you to write and use these diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit and counit of an adjunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Associated to an adjunction τ are maps η_A : A → G(F(A)) (the unit) and ϵ_B : F(G(B)) → B (the counit), constructed from τ by applying it to identities; these satisfy the usual compositions expressing how τ is implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises show how τAB(1_{F(A)}) gives η_A and τ^{-1}(1_{G(B)}) gives ϵ_B, and how to express τAB(g) and τ^{-1}(f) via compositions using η and ϵ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangle identities / characterization of adjunction via unit and counit
rubrics_metrics.description: If natural transformations η: id_A → G F and ϵ: F G → id_B satisfy the triangle identities (e.g., Gϵ ◦ ηG = id_G and ϵF ◦ Fη = id_F), then F is left-adjoint to G (and conversely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an alternative characterization of adjoints; check the identities directly (Exercise 1.5.1 / §1.5.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Key examples of adjoint pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Common adjoint pairs include tensor/Hom (⊗_A N left-adjoint to Hom_A(N, ·)), extension/restriction of scalars (· ⊗_B A left-adjoint to restriction), induction/restriction of representations (Ind ⊣ Res), suspension ⊣ loop space in topology, groupification ⊣ forgetful, sheaf pushforward/pullback pairs (π_! ⊣ π^* etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises (1.5.C–1.5.H) guide construction/verification of these examples; a table summarizes many adjoints that will appear later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoints preserve (co)limits: left adjoints commute with colimits, right adjoints with limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If (F,G) is an adjoint pair with F left-adjoint and G right-adjoint, then F commutes with colimits and G commutes with limits; more generally, limits commute with limits and colimits commute with colimits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated in §1.5.4 and reproved/extended in §1.6.12; use these facts to transfer exactness/commutation properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of additive category (Ad1–Ad3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category C is additive if (Ad1) Mor(A,B) is an abelian group and composition distributes over addition, (Ad2) C has a zero object, and (Ad3) C has finite products (hence finite coproducts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In additive categories Hom is often denoted Hom and morphisms are called homomorphisms. Additive functors preserve these structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and universal property of kernel and cokernel
rubrics_metrics.description: For f: B → C, a kernel is i: A → B with f ◦ i = 0 universal with this property (unique up to unique isomorphism); the cokernel is defined dually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kernels are limits and cokernels are colimits (see (1.6.3.1)); note kernel/cokernel are morphisms, not just objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: An abelian category is an additive category satisfying (1) every map has a kernel and cokernel, (2) every monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel, and (3) every epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many expected properties of kernels/cokernels/images follow from these three axioms (see remarks). Examples: Ab and Mod_A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image as ker(coker f)
rubrics_metrics.description: The image of a morphism f is defined (when it exists) as im(f) = ker(coker f); then f factors uniquely as A → im f → B with the first map epi and the second mono.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show im f is an epimorphism followed by a monomorphism; verifying this factorization is a useful exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: complex, exactness, and homology
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence ... → A →^f B →^g C → ... is a complex at B if g ◦ f = 0; it is exact at B if ker g = im f. The homology at B is H = ker g / im f (cycles mod boundaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short exact sequences are exact sequences of the form 0 → A → B → C → 0. Indexing conventions (cohomology as superscripts or subscripts) are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short exact sequence facts and factorization into short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: An exact sequence can be factored into short exact sequences (see (1.6.5.3) and (1.6.5.4)), which is often helpful for proofs about long exact sequences and homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises prompt you to write these factorizations explicitly and use them to deduce properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComC (category of complexes) is abelian
rubrics_metrics.description: For an abelian category C, the category ComC of complexes (objects are complexes, morphisms are commuting degreewise maps) is itself an abelian category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 1.6.C asks to prove this (special case Mod_A is often used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of functors: left-exact, right-exact, exact (covariant and contravariant)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covariant additive functor F is right-exact if F preserves the exactness at the right end of short exact sequences (A' → A → A'' → 0 implies F(A') → F(A) → F(A'') → 0 exact); left-exact is defined dually. Contravariant functors have analogous definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A functor is exact if it is both left- and right-exact. Exercises illustrate tensor/Hom/localization as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of modules is exact
rubrics_metrics.description: The localization functor Mod_A → Mod_{S^{-1}A} (S a multiplicative subset) is exact (Exercise 1.6.F(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently S^{-1}A is a flat A-algebra; localization commutes with cohomology of complexes of A-modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product is right-exact; Hom is left-exact
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed modules, · ⊗_A M is a right-exact covariant functor Mod_A → Mod_A, while Hom(C, ·) is left-exact (and similarly for other variants described in Exercise 1.6.F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motivates the notion of flatness (see next item) and leads to derived functors when left-exactness suggests higher terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHHF Theorem (interaction of homology and (left/right-)exact functors)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Exercise 1.6.H) For a covariant functor F between abelian categories and a complex C•: (a) if F is right-exact, there are natural morphisms F(H_i(C•)) → H_i(F(C•)); (b) if F is left-exact, natural morphisms H_i(F(C•)) → F(H_i(C•)); (c) if F is exact these are isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use behavior of cokernels and images under F to build the maps; special case: tensoring with N yields the usual statements relating ⊗ and homology and leads to flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness characterized by exactness of tensor
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module N is flat iff the functor N ⊗_A · is exact (i.e., both left- and right-exact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localization S^{-1}A is flat for all multiplicative sets S (corollary of exactness of localization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered colimits are exact in ModA
rubrics_metrics.description: In Mod_A, colimits over filtered index categories are exact (Exercise 1.6.K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text cautions this need not hold in arbitrary abelian categories (Grothendieck's AB5 addresses such issues); proofs often reduce to elementwise/local arguments like localization or stalkification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits commute with limits; colimits commute with colimits; adjoints preserve these behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits commute with limits and with right adjoints; colimits commute with colimits and with left adjoints. In particular, right adjoints are left-exact (kernels are limits) and left adjoints are right-exact (cokernels are colimits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.6.12 and Proposition 1.6.15 for proof sketches and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernels commute with limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Given diagrams a,b : I → C and a natural transformation h: a → b, the kernel objects ker(h_i) form a diagram whose limit is canonically isomorphic to ker(lim h_i) (Exercise 1.6.I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an instance of the general principle that limits commute with limits; use the universal properties to construct the isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right adjoints commute with limits (Proposition 1.6.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (F,G) is an adjoint pair F: C → D, G: D → C and A = lim_i A_i is a limit in D, then G(A) ≅ lim_i G(A_i) (with the corresponding maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses adjointness to translate maps into D and then the universal property of limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence in cohomology from a short exact sequence of complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence of complexes 0 → A• → B• → C• → 0 induces a long exact sequence ... → H^{i-1}(C•) → H^i(A•) → H^i(B•) → H^i(C•) → H^{i+1}(A•) → ... (Theorem 1.6.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction requires defining the connecting homomorphism; see Exercise 1.7.F or standard proofs (Snake Lemma).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagram chasing justified by Freyd–Mitchell Embedding Theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: If C is an abelian category with Hom(X,Y) sets, then C embeds exactly and fully into Mod_A for some ring A, justifying proofs by elementwise 'diagram-chasing' as if in modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References and caveats given; for reassurance one may use Mac Lane's elementary diagram-chasing rules as an alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology commutes with filtered colimits in ModA
rubrics_metrics.description: Filtered colimits commute with homology in Mod_A (Exercise 1.6.L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FHHF Theorem together with exactness of filtered colimits to prove this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of inverse limits under surjective transition maps
rubrics_metrics.description: For an inverse system of exact sequences of modules with surjective transition maps on the left terms (An+1 → An surjective), the limit sequence 0 → lim An → lim Bn → lim Cn → 0 is exact (Exercise 1.6.M / (1.6.15.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specific sufficient condition (a Mittag-Leffler-type hypothesis) ensuring exactness of inverse limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning: right-exact functors need not commute with infinite direct sums
rubrics_metrics.description: Right-exactness alone does not guarantee commuting with infinite direct sums; counterexample: the double-dual functor V ↦ V^{∨∨} is covariant and right-exact but does not commute with infinite direct sums in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Unimportant Remark 1.6.16 for the concrete counterexample and further discussion.
